title: Machine learning survival model predicts catheter-related thrombosis in tumour patients
summary: The SM-CRT survival model was built from prospectively collected catheterization data from 30,947 tumour patients across four centres. It reached c-indexes of 0.714 on the prospective test dataset and 0.678 and 0.779 on two external test datasets, and flagged femoral and peripherally inserted central catheters, thoracic tumours and alkylating agents as high-risk factors. The c-indexes are modest and the abstract reports risk stratification, not a trial of prevention.
organization: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cancer Hospital; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

evidence.tested: c-index on a prospective test dataset and two external test datasets, and event rates in predicted risk groups.
evidence.unknown: Modest c-indexes; whether model-guided prevention improves patient outcomes not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning survival model ranking catheter-related thrombosis risk and predicting survival distributions.
